findings.reason: I checked line 52: it now does `break` on backslash+space, so it returns str `foo` with pos on the `\`. In link.mjs:54-63, `start === pos`, so no title is parsed. Line 76 then sees `\` instead of `)` and falls back to reference parsing, which drops a link CommonMark treats as valid. I set it to medium, between C1's medium and X1's high. The trigger is real but the input is narrow, and nothing crashes and no security is affected.
findings.claim: An unbracketed destination ending in a backslash and then a space (e.g. `[x](foo\ "t")`, `[x](a\ )`, `[x]: a\ "t"`) no longer parses as a link. It renders as literal text.
findings.evidence: The diff changes `if (str.charCodeAt(pos + 1) === 0x20) { pos++; continue }` to `{ break }`. Before the change, the backslash stayed in the destination and the next loop pass stopped at the space (`if (code === 0x20) { break }`), so the result was `a\`. Now the loop stops before the backslash, so the result is `a` and `res.pos` points at `\`. In lib/rules_inline/link.mjs:55-63, the parser skips no whitespace (`start === pos`), so no title is parsed. Line 76 then sees `\` where it expects `)` and sets `parseReference = true`, which drops the inline link. lib/rules_block/reference.mjs uses the same helper, so reference definitions are affected the same way.
